rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 describe a 2011-2013 split-plot field experiment with four replications at Kruszyn Krajenski, central Poland, on very light soil (own data). Q2: Section 3.2 and Table 6 report that nitrogen fertigation, averaged over years, significantly raised marketable tuber yield from 28.85 to 32.28 t/ha (about 12%); Table 8 reports tuber number per plant rising from 10.3 to 12.8 with fertigation; Table 6 also shows drip irrigation raising yield from 22.61 to 38.53 t/ha (55%).
rows.notes: Study directly matches the claim (fertigation vs broadcasting yield and tuber number increases; 3.43/28.85 = 11.9%, 2.5/10.3 = 24.3%). Q3 no: only harvested yield and tuber counts from the same trial, one method. Q4 doubtful: authors measured yield components (tuber weight, number) and a yield-tuber weight correlation (r = 0.912), but no measurement of soil N, plant N uptake or soil water as intermediate variables for the fertigation effect; mechanism (optimal nutrient concentration in wet zone) is cited from other work, so rated no. Q5 no: one site, one soil, one cultivar. Q6 no: 11.25 m2 plots. Q7 no: no condition stated from own findings as a requirement; remarks on light soils and rainfall effects are cited or interactions. Q8 no: no limitations of own result stated. Q9 no: only Tukey letter groupings and significance stars; no SD, SE, CI or range for the yield or tuber-number effect.

notes: Full text available; some tables duplicated by PDF extraction but readable. Single field experiment in central Poland 2011-2013 on potato cv. Courage with drip irrigation x nitrogen fertigation.
